default.title: comma four setup
default.summary: Install your comma four in five steps.

steps.title: Remove the rearview mirror cover trim
body: Check the cover release method for your model and year before removing it. Keep the camera attached to the windshield.
The photos show an example installation; covers and connector positions vary by vehicle.

steps.title: Connect car harness into the camera
body: Unplug the existing LKAS camera connector and plug it into the harness.
Connect the other end of the harness back into the LKAS camera.
Connect the small car-harness connector to the harness box and make sure it is fully seated.
Find a spot for the harness box so the trim can still fit over it. Peel off the adhesive backing and attach the box in place.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Reinstall the rearview mirror cover trim
body: Make sure the car harness fully fits inside the trim.
Generally, it is best to have the OBD-C cable come out of the top.

power_instructions: Plug comma power into the vehicle's OBD-II port. Route its cable clear of pedals and airbag deployment paths.
Connect its small 4-pin plug to the matching socket on the harness box.

Audi A3 2014-19.title: Audi A3
Audi A3 2014-19.summary: Your VW J533 connector connects at the gateway. Follow the vehicle-specific steps below.

steps.title: Access the gateway under the dashboard
body: Turn the vehicle off before disconnecting the gateway.
The J533 gateway is usually above the driver's footwell. Confirm its location for your vehicle; remove the lower dashboard trim only if needed.
Identify the gateway and release its connector locking mechanism before unplugging it.

steps.title: Connect the harness at the gateway
body: Unplug the vehicle connector at the gateway and plug it into the matching end of your car harness.
Plug the other end of the harness back into the gateway. Make sure the connector locks are fully engaged.
Connect the small car-harness connector to the harness box and make sure it is fully seated.
Secure the harness box where the trim can fit back in place without pinching any cables.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Route the long OBD-C cable from the harness box to the windshield. Keep it clear of pedals, moving parts, and airbag deployment paths.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Secure the cable and reinstall the trim
body: Secure excess cable so it cannot move into pedals, seat rails, or other moving parts. Keep airbag deployment paths clear.
Check that the harness and cable fit behind the panels, then reinstall the trim you removed.

notes: Gateway access can vary by model and steering configuration; right-hand-drive access has not been verified for every model.
power_instructions: Plug comma power into the vehicle's OBD-II port. Route its cable clear of pedals and airbag deployment paths.
Connect its small 4-pin plug to the matching socket on the harness box.

steps.title: Remove the camera cover
body: Remove the cover behind the rearview mirror to expose the forward-facing camera connector.
Use the harness listed for your exact model, year, region, and HDA II equipment.
Some Hyundai harnesses fit the same connector but have different wiring; do not substitute one based on appearance alone.

steps.title: Connect car harness into the camera
body: Locate the connector plugged directly into the forward-facing lane-keeping camera.
Release its locking tab, unplug it from the camera, and plug it into the harness.
Connect the other end of the harness back into the LKAS camera.
Connect the small car-harness connector to the harness box and make sure it is fully seated.
Find a spot for the harness box so the trim can still fit over it. Peel off the adhesive backing and attach the box in place.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Reinstall the rearview mirror cover trim
body: Make sure the car harness fully fits inside the trim.
Generally, it is best to have the OBD-C cable come out of the top.

power_instructions: Plug comma power into the vehicle's OBD-II port. Route its cable clear of pedals and airbag deployment paths.
Connect its small 4-pin plug to the matching socket on the harness box.

Rivian R1S 2022-24.title: Rivian R1S
Rivian R1S 2022-24.summary: Your Rivian A connector connects at the AXM. Follow the vehicle-specific steps below.

steps.title: Access the AXM in the passenger footwell
body: Put the Rivian to sleep before unplugging any connectors. Turn off Gear Guard, open the passenger door, lock the vehicle, and leave the door ajar.
Turn off your phone's Bluetooth and disconnect it from the vehicle's Wi-Fi hotspot. Keep the key fob out of range and walk away for 15–20 minutes.
Return from the passenger side. Verify that all screens remain off during harness installation, and do not put weight on either front seat.
Remove the passenger footwell trim to reach the AXM driver-assistance module and identify its connector using the reference photos.
The white connector in front of the AXM can be temporarily disconnected for access; it is separate from the harness connection.

steps.title: Connect the harness at the AXM
body: Unplug the vehicle connector at the AXM and plug it into the matching end of your car harness.
Plug the other end of the harness back into the AXM. Make sure the connector locks are fully engaged.
Connect the small car-harness connector to the harness box and make sure it is fully seated.
Secure the harness box where the trim can fit back in place without pinching any cables.

Reconnect any connector temporarily removed for access, including the white connector, and check all connector locks. Once the vehicle connections are restored, wake the Rivian before connecting the comma four.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the device below the rearview mirror itself, not the larger Mobileye housing, which is offset.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Route the long OBD-C cable from the passenger footwell through the dash side-panel opening, along the windshield side of the A-pillar trim, and toward the windshield mount. Keep it clear of pedals, moving parts, and airbag deployment paths.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Secure the cable and reinstall the trim
body: Secure excess cable so it cannot move into pedals, seat rails, or other moving parts. Keep airbag deployment paths clear.
Check that the harness and cable fit behind the panels, then reinstall the trim you removed.

notes: The comma Rivian harness receives power at the AXM. Before adding comma power, ask comma support to verify the power configuration for your harness revision. The linked installation references disagree about whether AXM power must be isolated when using comma power; the preparation reference warns of electrical backfeeding when both sources are connected.
power_instructions: Plug comma power into the vehicle's OBD-II port. Route its cable clear of pedals and airbag deployment paths.
Connect its small 4-pin plug to the matching socket on the harness box.

Subaru Ascent 2019-21.title: Subaru Ascent
Subaru Ascent 2019-21.summary: Install your comma four with the Subaru A connector.

steps.title: Remove the EyeSight cover
body: Check the cover removal procedure for your model year before pulling on the overhead EyeSight cover. Remove its retaining bolts before releasing the clips and hooks; their locations vary by cover.
Use a plastic trim tool and the listed 8 mm deep socket. Leave the camera assembly installed. Do not touch or attempt to clean the EyeSight lenses; keep tools and loose wiring away from them.

steps.title: Connect the harness to EyeSight
body: Confirm the harness matches the one listed for your exact vehicle. Subaru A and B have the same connector housings but different wiring, so physical fit alone is not enough. Release the EyeSight connector latch and connect the vehicle wiring to the harness.
Connect the other end back to EyeSight and make sure both connector locks are fully engaged.
Connect the small car-harness connector to the harness box and make sure it is fully seated.
Find a spot for the harness box so the trim can still fit over it. Peel off the adhesive backing and attach the box in place.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Before peeling the mount backing, hold comma four and its cable in position. Keep both EyeSight cameras' views clear and check the prohibited accessory areas in your vehicle's EyeSight manual. Leave room to remove the EyeSight cover later.
Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Reinstall the EyeSight cover
body: Secure the harness clear of the EyeSight cameras, cover fasteners, and moving sunroof components. Keep wiring away from bolt holes and make sure the cover fits without pinching any cables.
Route the OBD-C cable toward the comma four and reinstall the cover.
Check that the cover sits evenly around both camera lenses and confirm normal EyeSight operation after installation.

notes: Cover clips and bolt access vary by model year. Detailed procedures labeled 2019 apply only to the named 2019 models; use your model year's illustrated procedure for other covers. The wiki's modern Subaru D harness instructions do not describe the Subaru A/B installation.
power_instructions: Plug comma power into the vehicle's OBD-II port. Route its cable clear of pedals and airbag deployment paths.
Connect its small 4-pin plug to the matching socket on the harness box.

body: Check the cover removal procedure for your model year before pulling on the overhead EyeSight cover. Remove its retaining bolts before releasing the clips and hooks; their locations vary by cover.
Use a plastic trim tool and the listed 8 mm deep socket. Leave the camera assembly installed. Do not touch or attempt to clean the EyeSight lenses; keep tools and loose wiring away from them.

steps.title: Connect the harness to EyeSight
body: Confirm the harness matches the one listed for your exact vehicle. Subaru A and B have the same connector housings but different wiring, so physical fit alone is not enough. Release the EyeSight connector latch and connect the vehicle wiring to the harness.
Connect the other end back to EyeSight and make sure both connector locks are fully engaged.
Connect the small car-harness connector to the harness box and make sure it is fully seated.
Find a spot for the harness box so the trim can still fit over it. Peel off the adhesive backing and attach the box in place.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Before peeling the mount backing, hold comma four and its cable in position. Keep both EyeSight cameras' views clear and check the prohibited accessory areas in your vehicle's EyeSight manual. Leave room to remove the EyeSight cover later.
Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Reinstall the EyeSight cover
body: Secure the harness clear of the EyeSight cameras, cover fasteners, and moving sunroof components. Keep wiring away from bolt holes and make sure the cover fits without pinching any cables.
Route the OBD-C cable toward the comma four and reinstall the cover.
Check that the cover sits evenly around both camera lenses and confirm normal EyeSight operation after installation.

notes: Cover clips and bolt access vary by model year. Detailed procedures labeled 2019 apply only to the named 2019 models; use your model year's illustrated procedure for other covers. The wiki's modern Subaru D harness instructions do not describe the Subaru A/B installation.
power_instructions: Plug comma power into the vehicle's OBD-II port. Route its cable clear of pedals and airbag deployment paths.
Connect its small 4-pin plug to the matching socket on the harness box.

Škoda Fabia 2022-23.title: Škoda Fabia
Škoda Fabia 2022-23.summary: Your VW J533 connector connects at the gateway. Follow the vehicle-specific steps below.

steps.title: Access the gateway under the dashboard
body: Turn the vehicle off before disconnecting the gateway.
The J533 gateway is usually above the driver's footwell. Confirm its location for your vehicle; remove the lower dashboard trim only if needed.
Identify the gateway and release its connector locking mechanism before unplugging it.

steps.title: Connect the harness at the gateway
body: Unplug the vehicle connector at the gateway and plug it into the matching end of your car harness.
Plug the other end of the harness back into the gateway. Make sure the connector locks are fully engaged.
Connect the small car-harness connector to the harness box and make sure it is fully seated.
Secure the harness box where the trim can fit back in place without pinching any cables.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Route the long OBD-C cable from the harness box to the windshield. Keep it clear of pedals, moving parts, and airbag deployment paths.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Secure the cable and reinstall the trim
body: Secure excess cable so it cannot move into pedals, seat rails, or other moving parts. Keep airbag deployment paths clear.
Check that the harness and cable fit behind the panels, then reinstall the trim you removed.

notes: Gateway access can vary by model and steering configuration; right-hand-drive access has not been verified for every model.
power_instructions: Plug comma power into the vehicle's OBD-II port. Route its cable clear of pedals and airbag deployment paths.
Connect its small 4-pin plug to the matching socket on the harness box.

Tesla Model 3 (with HW2.5) 2019.title: Tesla Model 3 (with HW2.5)
Tesla Model 3 (with HW2.5) 2019.summary: Your Tesla A connector connects at the Autopilot computer. Follow the vehicle-specific steps below.

steps.title: Access the Autopilot computer in the passenger footwell
body: Confirm the shutdown and isolation procedure described in the installation notes before disconnecting any computer connectors.

Use the model-specific reference to remove the passenger footwell trim and any adjoining panels needed for access. Keep track of electrical connections removed with the panels so they can be restored.
Use the Tesla A connector supplied for your selected vehicle and the HW3 connection reference below.

steps.title: Connect the harness at the Autopilot computer
body: Identify the connection shown in the HW3 reference before unplugging it. The Tesla A and Tesla B connection locations differ.
Release the connector lock and insert the matching car harness between the vehicle connector and the Autopilot computer. Make sure both connector locks are fully engaged.
Connect the small car-harness connector to the harness box and make sure it is fully seated.
Restore any adjacent connectors removed for access. Secure the harness box where the trim can fit without pinching cables.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Route the long OBD-C cable from the harness box to the windshield. Keep it clear of pedals, moving parts, and airbag deployment paths.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Secure the cable and reinstall the trim
body: Restore all electrical connections removed for access, including any footwell-panel connections.
Follow the confirmed model-specific procedure to restore power and wake the vehicle. Before reinstalling the trim, verify that comma four starts and the vehicle reports no new errors.
Secure excess cable clear of pedals, seat rails, moving parts, and airbag deployment paths. Check that the harness and cable fit behind the panels, then reinstall the trim.

notes: Before unplugging the Autopilot computer, confirm the shutdown and electrical isolation procedure for your exact model and hardware with the harness maker or Tesla service documentation. Volkswagen Arteon 2018-23.title: Volkswagen Arteon
Volkswagen Arteon 2018-23.summary: Your VW J533 connector connects at the gateway. Follow the vehicle-specific steps below.

steps.title: Access the gateway under the dashboard
body: Turn the vehicle off before disconnecting the gateway.
The J533 gateway is usually above the driver's footwell. Confirm its location for your vehicle; remove the lower dashboard trim only if needed.
Identify the gateway and release its connector locking mechanism before unplugging it.

steps.title: Connect the harness at the gateway
body: Unplug the vehicle connector at the gateway and plug it into the matching end of your car harness.
Plug the other end of the harness back into the gateway. Make sure the connector locks are fully engaged.
Connect the small car-harness connector to the harness box and make sure it is fully seated.
Secure the harness box where the trim can fit back in place without pinching any cables.

steps.title: Place mount high and centered on the windshield
body: Clean the mounting area with the included alcohol wipe and let it dry.
Leave enough room for the cable when the device is mounted, and make sure you can see the screen from a seated position.
Center the mount horizontally so the device can properly center in the lane.
Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Route the long OBD-C cable from the harness box to the windshield. Keep it clear of pedals, moving parts, and airbag deployment paths.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Secure the cable and reinstall the trim
body: Secure excess cable so it cannot move into pedals, seat rails, or other moving parts. Keep airbag deployment paths clear.
Check that the harness and cable fit behind the panels, then reinstall the trim you removed.

notes: Gateway access can vary by model and steering configuration; right-hand-drive access has not been verified for every model.
power_instructions: Plug comma power into the vehicle's OBD-II port. Route its cable clear of pedals and airbag deployment paths.
Connect its small 4-pin plug to the matching socket on the harness box.

Peel off the mount's tape cover. Press firmly in the center, then the edges. Make sure no bubbles form.

steps.title: Plug in OBD-C and mount the device
body: Route the long OBD-C cable from the harness box to the windshield. Keep it clear of pedals, moving parts, and airbag deployment paths.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the harness box. Make sure the cable is fully seated.
Plug the OBD-C cable into the comma four. Make sure the cable is all the way in.
Slide the device onto the mount until it is fully seated.

steps.title: Secure the cable and reinstall the trim
body: Secure excess cable so it cannot move into pedals, seat rails, or other moving parts. Keep airbag deployment paths clear.
Check that the harness and cable fit behind the panels, then reinstall the trim you removed.

notes: Gateway access can vary by model and steering configuration; right-hand-drive access has not been verified for every model.
power_instructions: Plug comma power into the vehicle's OBD-II port. Route its cable clear of pedals and airbag deployment paths.
Connect its small 4-pin plug to the matching socket on the harness box.
